$comment: Gemfall beat 4 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 4A). The opening reads the `crossing` set from 03a through requiresFlag on two extra choices beside an ungated road: crossed_dry parties ride in with the caravans, river_took_us parties walk up from the mouth-lands and see the bent routes first (saw_the_bend, the wet door's witness dividend). Sets no carried flag. The setback needs a party that took the Pride Stone to camp alone, then fail the wolf check or pick the fight, and lose it. The expansion's spine episodes (brass rope, relay runner, cub scouts, granny cake, nap vote, moving marker, dawn moths, jackalope wall, wolf sign) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Pride Roads

plate.narration: In the Eastern Plains, a manticore watches a road that bends far out through the grass. Fresh earth clings to the old route markers. Even the caravans are taking the long way round. Something has made pride country uneasy.

objectives.label: Saw how the pride routes bend

goal.text: Cross pride country and find out why its roads bend the long way around.

steps.label: Find what the roads bend around

facet_pride.name: The Pride Stone
facet_pride.text: From the fall no pride will den within a day of. Heavy, warm, and humming.

scene_east_bank.narration: Cross pride country and find out why its roads bend the long way around. The Eastern Plains roll away in gold grass. Far north, the big river bridge is cracked. Every caravan is taking a detour. The wind smells a little of lion.

scene_caravan_dry.narration: You join the caravans from Stone Crossing. Parsnip the donkey's driver is furious. "The pride escort won't camp at the usual rest stop!" Parsnip sleeps by the gem crates. She agrees with the prides.

scene_mouthlands_walk.narration: Walking up from the south, you see it first: the pride markers, replanted in a curve, like a road walking around a hot pan. Old Ossley's reed knot is still wet in your pocket. You owe that frog a favor.

scene_pride_road.narration: Pride markers line the road: painted posts with tufts of tail-fur on top. You walk around them, never over. Overhead, embermoths drift south, away from the mountain. Embermoths never do that.

scene_embermoths.narration: The glowing moths lead you along the grass. The pride markers curve the same way, around something you can't see yet. Forty jackalopes have squashed together by the road. It is mostly ears.

scene_bend_from_above.narration: From up high, the plains are a map. The pride roads used to run straight as string. Now every one bends wide around the same patch of grass, like you tiptoe past a sleeping dog.

scene_pride_greeting.narration: A manticore elder named Sefa greets you, her tail curled politely away. "Welcome, travelers," she says. "Greet us back properly, and you may sit at our fire."

check_greeting.prompt: Wave first, slowly and kindly, the way the road peoples do

onSuccess.narration: Palm open, slow, from far off. The elder looks delighted, and waves you all the way up to the fire.

onFailure.narration: Everybody waves at once with both arms, like people drowning in grass. The elder blinks, decides you meant well, and lets you sit at the edge of camp.

scene_hospitality.narration: The elder sees you and drops the formal greeting. "Look who's come home the front way!" Cubs pile on you. Somebody's grandmother hands you a honeycake, whether you want one or not.

scene_pride_camp.narration: "My cubs dream of humming near gem wagons," says Elder Sefa Tallgrass. "So we den farther away. The centaur wardens at the waystation map every road. After nap time, I will send you there."

scene_riddle_account.narration: Sefa keeps a riddle score with Old Lintel, the toll-troll at Stone Crossing. You could write Lintel's question in her ledger: where did it come from, and where is it going? Or try their oldest riddle.

check_old_riddle.prompt: Answer the riddle nobody has solved in sixty years

onSuccess.narration: You say your answer. The whole pride goes silent. Then Sefa writes it down very carefully, and two cubs sprint off to tell everybody. You will be famous at both ends of the bridge, and argued about forever.

onFailure.narration: You guess "a teapot." It is not a teapot. Several famous careers have ended on that riddle, so you are in very good company.

scene_waystation.narration: At the centaur waystation, road maps are stitched onto long sashes. A road-warden waves you over, spools in her mouth. "Every sash needs changing this season," she mutters. "Help me see why."

check_sashes.narration: The warden lights a lantern behind each sash. "The new detours glow in the order the stones fell," she says. "Watch, then put them back in order."

interaction.cue: Watch the roads glow, then stitch them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Sash by sash, you line them up. The warden drops her spools. "Oh."

onFailure.narration: The sashes tangle into a woolly knot. The warden untangles it and lays them out.

onAssisted.narration: The warden holds the lanterns steady. Sash by sash, you line them up.

scene_spiral.narration: Side by side, the new detours are not random. They spiral. Every road bends around the places where the stones fell, like water around rocks. The roads are flinching from the stones. The widest spiral centers on a patch of grass not far from here.

rest_waystation.narration: The centaurs feed you oat-cakes and pack you a supper bundle. Then they argue about whose stitching is neatest. "Mine," sniffs the warden. Rest a while in the hay.

rest_waystation_with_escort.narration: At dawn, Elder Sefa walks out with you, and two cubs, because nobody told them not to. Ahead, the grass leans away from something. Sefa stops. "We always wait here," she says.

scene_widest_bend.narration: At the widest bend, a humming gem sits in a little crater. The grass leans away from it. Take it, and the pride must keep its distance tonight. Leave it, and they will welcome you at their fire.

scene_take_stone.narration: The Pride Stone is heavy and warm. It hums right through your fingers. The pride walks back with you, but farther off than before. Tonight they cannot camp near you. They are very sorry.

scene_leave_stone.narration: You leave it humming in its crater. When you turn around, Elder Sefa is on the ridge. She bows, slow and deep. "Come to the fire," she says.

scene_wolves.narration: You camp at the old caravan rest stop, among empty carts. Out in the dark: ember eyes. Cinder wolves, thin and cold, creep toward your fire. They hate the humming. They love the warm.

check_wolves.prompt: Throw supper far enough that the pack takes the easy meal

onSuccess.narration: The supper lands in the grass and the pack pours after it. When they come back they are full, and they lie down on the far side of the fire like big glowing dogs.

onFailure.narration: They take the supper. Then they come back for the fire.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves circle the old carts, trying to get between you and the warm.

onVictory.narration: The pack backs off into one glowing heap. You are too much bother.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves want the fire more than you do. In the end, they simply take it.

rest_pride_fire.narration: Pride fire is the best fire. The cubs fall asleep on your boots. Out in the dark, the stone you left hums alone. Tomorrow, north to the broken bridge.

variants.text: The warden helped pin the sashes.

rest_wolf_fire.narration: By midnight the cinder wolves are stacked in a glowing pile across the fire. It is the warmest camp ever. Tomorrow, north to the broken bridge.

variants.text: The warden helped pin the sashes.

rest_scattered.narration: Nobody is hurt. The wolves just wanted the warm more than you did. You sleep under a cart cover. By morning, your camp is spread across a mile of grass. The Pride Stone hums, not sorry at all.

variants.text: The warden helped pin the sashes.

scene_escort_answers.narration: You call toward the ridge. Elder Sefa answers from the dark, and the cubs growl so low you feel it in your boots. The wolves think it over, and slink to the far side of camp.

scene_brass_rope.narration: Six people in brass hats have stretched a rope across the road. "Brassbuckle Expedition toll," says their scout. "Brand new. Very official." They want your coins. The rope is tied to nothing much.

scene_brass_rope_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get that rope?" you ask, the way Old Lintel would. "And where is this road going?" Nobody knows. "Tuesday?" says their recordkeeper. They take the rope down quietly.

scene_brass_rope_walk_round.narration: You walk around the end of the rope, slow and polite, the pride way. The rope stops nobody. It is just a rope in a field. Behind you, the Brassbuckles argue about fences.

scene_brass_rope_whose_road.narration: "This is a pride road," you say, tail curled politely away. "It was here before your hats." Manticore ears pop up all along the ridge. The rope comes down very fast.

scene_relay_runner.narration: A centaur skids up, her sash stuffed with letters. "Bracken Swiftmile, relay runner!" she pants. "News from the west? News going north? Quick. The relay waits for nobody."

scene_relay_runner_news_west.narration: "West road's strange," says Bracken. "Marsh lights gossip about a humming gate. Witches' bells ring when a gem goes by. Every stone is humming!" Then she is gone in a cloud of dust.

check_race.prompt: The fastest of you races a relay centaur to the next pride post

onSuccess.narration: You run like the wind, and the wind is impressed. You touch the post one breath before Bracken does, mostly because she was laughing too hard to run properly. "Fair's fair," she says, and tells you all the relay news for free: on every road in the realm, the stones are humming.

onFailure.narration: Bracken is a centaur. She reaches the post, reads her letters, eats an apple, and waves you in. "Not bad for two legs," she says kindly, and tells you the relay news anyway: on every road in the realm, the stones are humming.

scene_relay_runner_carry_letters.narration: Bracken hands you letters for the centaur waystation up the road. You fly them ahead and drop them on the big table. Later she tells every centaur in the barn about you. Twice.

scene_cub_scouts.narration: Two rocks on the ridge are breathing. They have ears and tufted tails. They are manticore cubs, pretending very hard. One giggles. "We are rocks," it whispers.

scene_cub_scouts_pretend.narration: You walk past, saying loudly what nice rocks these are. The rocks are thrilled. They follow you, ducking whenever you turn, then gallop ahead to say they caught some visitors.

scene_cub_scouts_play_rocks.narration: You become rocks too. A beetle crosses your boot. "You moved!" shouts a cub. You did not. The cubs win anyway, because they made the rules.

scene_cub_scouts_ask_why.narration: "Why does the road go the long way?" you ask. The rocks forget to be rocks. "Because of the humming," says the big one. "It makes us dream the ground sings." Then they freeze again.

scene_pride_greeting_cubs_introduce.narration: The cubs march you up to the elder like prizes. "We caught them!" says the big one. You and the elder keep perfectly straight faces. "Then they had better come to the fire," she says.

scene_granny_cake.narration: Granny Ash, a manticore grandmother, blocks the fire with a plate of spiced grass-cake. "Nobody has ever finished a slice," she says proudly. The cubs want to see you try.

check_cake.prompt: Finish a slice of Granny Ash's spiced grass-cake

onSuccess.narration: Bite. Chew. Your eyes water. Your ears go hot. Bite. Chew. You swallow the last crumb, and the whole pride roars. Granny Ash pats your head and announces to the ridge that you are family now, and nobody is allowed to argue.

onFailure.narration: Bite, chew, and steam comes out of your ears. Actual steam. You have to stop halfway and drink a whole bucket of water. Granny Ash is delighted. She has never seen anyone steam before, and she tells everybody, all evening.

scene_granny_cake_recipe.narration: Granny Ash recites the ingredients. One of them seems to be thunder. The cubs are very impressed. Then she asks you to help carry the plates.

scene_granny_cake_share_back.narration: You open your packs to find her a gift. The humming gets louder, and Granny Ash steps back without meaning to. "It's not you, dear," she says. "It's whatever is singing in there."

choice_cub_nap.narration: Nap time. But the cubs stare at your humming packs and cannot sleep. "I have tried counting cubs," Sefa sighs. "They keep changing places." How will you help them sleep?

choice_cub_nap_packs_away.narration: You carry the humming packs far out of camp, and the cubs fall asleep. Around the packs, the grass leans away. You trace that edge for tomorrow, then fetch the packs back.

check_lullaby.prompt: Everybody sing two manticore cubs to sleep over the hum

onSuccess.narration: You sing the slowest, softest song you know, and then you sing it again. The cubs' eyes go heavy. One by one they flop over into a warm furry pile, purring, and Elder Sefa mouths a silent thank you over the top of them.

onFailure.narration: Everybody starts singing a different song at once. It is so awful that the cubs laugh until they are worn out, and fall asleep in a heap, still giggling. Elder Sefa says that counts.

choice_cub_nap_lintel_story.narration: You tell the cubs about Old Lintel, the mossy troll who asks everybody, "Where did you get that? And where is it going?" They fall asleep asking it in smaller and smaller voices.

choice_cub_nap_reed_knot.narration: You wind Old Ossley's wet reed knot around your packs. The hum goes soft, like a far-off river. The cubs are asleep in a minute. Sefa raises one eyebrow, and does not ask.

scene_moving_marker.narration: Near camp, two manticores are moving a heavy pride marker farther from the caravan road. "Hands welcome," puffs one. Carry it, and they will teach you to brace a long load. Or ask where the new line goes.

check_marker_post.prompt: Everybody take a corner of a pride marker post and carry it to its new hole

onSuccess.narration: You heave the post up between you and march it out to the new spot, further from the caravan road. It arrives at the hole without a wobble, tuft and all.

onFailure.narration: The post is heavier than it looks, and it looks very heavy. You wobble all the way there, and it ends up leaning against the hole like a tired giraffe.

scene_moving_marker_ask_where.narration: "Farther from the caravans," says a mover. She walks you along the old holes. Between them, the grass leans outward, a line you could follow tomorrow. The post still needs planting.

scene_moving_marker_fly_line.narration: From up high you see the new hole, the old holes and older holes, each farther from the caravan road. Something is pushing the markers out. The manticores just nod. They know.

scene_waystation_stitch_first.narration: You help pin a sash flat on a frame first. Then the clues stay where everyone can see them. The warden takes out a spool, so nobody mistakes it for a button.

scene_waystation_letters_arrived.narration: The whole barn turns around. "The griffin from the letters!" The warden takes the spools out of her mouth to shake your hand. Bracken's letters are already pinned on the wall.

scene_spiral_mark_falls.narration: You mark each fall in red. Every road bends away from the dots. The map looks like it has measles. The warden hangs it up where everyone can see.

scene_dawn_moths.narration: At dawn, embermoths drift south in a glowing river, away from the mountain. One bumps your pack and darts off. The sky is orange in the wrong place.

scene_dawn_moths_let_pass.narration: You stand still while the moths swerve around your packs. The last ones hurry south. A few small lights are left behind in the grass.

check_moth.prompt: Cup an embermoth in your hands without squashing it

onSuccess.narration: You cup one, as gently as a bubble. It is shivering. Embermoths love warm and love the mountain, and this one is flying away from both. You hold it till it stops shaking, then let it go, south, with all the others.

onFailure.narration: You miss. You miss again. On the third try an embermoth lands on your nose all by itself, glows very brightly, and makes you sneeze. Then it hurries south after the others, away from the mountain, as fast as it can go.

scene_jackalope_wall.narration: A wall of jackalope ears blocks the bend. Every jackalope faces away from the middle. The oldest has one torn ear and a very firm opinion of you.

check_jackalopes.prompt: Everybody crawl through a wall of jackalopes without stepping on anybody

onSuccess.narration: Hands, knees, hands, knees, and "excuse me" fifty times. Not one toe is stepped on. When you come out the far side, every jackalope turns its head to watch you go, the way you watch someone walk into a cold sea.

onFailure.narration: Hands, knees, and then somebody puts a hand on a tail. One jackalope squeaks, and all fifty jump at once, straight up, like popcorn, and land again in exactly the same places. You crawl the rest of the way pink with embarrassment.

scene_jackalope_wall_ask_oldest.narration: The oldest thumps: thump, thump, pause, thump. The line opens, then closes behind you. You think that meant "on your own head be it."

scene_jackalope_wall_honeycake.narration: You break a honeycake into fifty tiny pieces. The jackalopes eat every crumb, then shuffle aside. A few little ones try to follow you. Their mothers pull them back by the ears.

scene_wolf_sign.narration: Warm paw prints cross a patch of ash. A cinder wolf has wandered far from home. Its prints curve around and around something. A cub would want to follow them, and a cub should not.

check_wolf_prints.prompt: Track a cinder wolf through leaning grass

onSuccess.narration: The prints go around, and around, in a wide careful circle, and never once step toward the middle. Even a cinder wolf, which loves anything hot, has walked the long way around. The circle leads you, at last, to the very middle of the bend.

onFailure.narration: You follow the prints around and around until you realize you are following your own boot prints, following the wolf's. Embarrassing. You give up and walk straight in, and find the very middle of the bend all on your own.

scene_wolf_sign_cover_prints.narration: You scuff the warm ash into the grass until nothing is left. Then you walk into the middle of the bend, where the grass leans farthest of all.

scene_waystation_lesson.narration: Your coin buys the warden's ready-made tags. "River first, then pride, bridge, pride," she says, pinning them up. Now you can compare clues instead of remembering lantern flashes.

interaction_ridge_creep.narration: The ridge path climbs through tall grass, and prides like to know who is coming. The grass hides your steps only while the wind rushes. When it stops, freeze.

interaction.cue: Tap to creep only while the wind is rushing through the grass.

onSuccess.narration: Step, rush, freeze, step. Not one rustle.

onFailure.narration: Crunch! A twig snaps under your boot. Somewhere ahead, something small snorts with laughter.

onAssisted.narration: The wind rushes at just the right moments. Not one rustle.

interaction_plates.narration: You help Granny Ash carry plates down the long table. A cub guards each slice until its owner sits down. Granny Ash tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

interaction_post_hole.narration: The movers hold the post while you guide it in. It goes in straight. The smaller one pays you three coins. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

interaction_lost_moths.narration: The glowing river has gone. But a few little moths got left behind. They huddle in the grass, flickering, too scared to fly alone.

scene_mud_posts.narration: Two marker posts stand by the muddy path. Nobody planted them. One blinks, and burps up a boot. Mire mimics! They collect pride tufts and boots, and they like the look of yours.

encounter_mimics.narration: The posts pull up out of the mud on short wet legs and shuffle toward your boots. Stomp them back into mud!

scene_mimics_unmasked.narration: The mimics slump into mud and cough up boots, hats, tufts and a brave whistle. You leave the tufts by the road for the cubs. The way to the bend is clear.

scene_mimics_took_boots.narration: The mimics win your boots. Then cubs arrive with sticks and hook them out of the mud, laughing. Your boots are muddy, but safe.

interaction_cub_lullaby.narration: The cubs need a soft sound. Each hero adds a hum, a gentle beat or a sleepy word. Say it out loud if you like. Sefa keeps the cubs' tails from drumming on the bowls.

interaction_marker_load.narration: Raise or lower your end until the post is level. Then carry it to the new hole. A tuft of tail-fur tickles somebody's nose.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the marker post.

onSuccess.narration: Level all the way! The movers teach you their long brace. It could steady a windbreak.

onFailure.narration: You wobble all the way. The post leans on its hole like a tired giraffe.

onAssisted.narration: A mover props the heavy end. You learn their long brace, good for a windbreak.

interaction_sash_frame.narration: Hold the sash flat while the acting hero pins its tags. Alone, use the frame. The warden calls out landmarks.

interaction.cue: Hold the sash flat while the acting hero pins its tags.

onSuccess.narration: The tags stay put. Now share the clues and line up the roads.

onFailure.narration: The pins slip. The warden reaches for her lanterns instead. Watch closely.

onAssisted.narration: The warden holds a corner while you pin. The tags stay put.

interaction_sashes_pinned.narration: Read the pinned tags together. River, pride, bridge and another pride road fit into one picture. The warden's spools sit safe in a cup.

interaction.cue: Share the pinned clues and line up four road sections.
clues: A pride road follows the river, then the bridge road.
A second pride section is last. Use the pride tag twice.

onSuccess.narration: The four roads line up. Now you see the whole shape.

onFailure.narration: The warden moves a few tags. With her help, you see the shape.

onAssisted.narration: The warden checks each tag with you. Together you line them up.

interaction_wolf_trail.narration: The wolf's warm prints glow in the swaying grass. Follow the last one, not your own boot prints!

interaction.cue: Follow the warm print and choose its final position.

onSuccess.narration: The prints circle wide to a crater. The wolf never went near its middle.

onFailure.narration: Those are your own boot prints! A giggling cub points out the crater.

onAssisted.narration: A breeze parts the grass. You follow the wolf's wide circle to a crater.

scene_pride_checked_line.narration: You follow the leaning grass you traced earlier. No tracking needed. At its widest curve, the line opens onto a little crater.

interaction_pride_windbreak.narration: A cart cover keeps flopping into the fire. Hold the long brace while the acting hero fixes it. Leave the wolves a warm patch, away from the humming packs.

interaction.cue: Hold the long brace while the acting hero fixes the windbreak.

onSuccess.narration: The cover holds, and the wolves settle in their warm patch.

onFailure.narration: The cover drops. The wolves still want the fire. Here they come!

onAssisted.narration: A wagon wheel props the brace. The cover holds, and the wolves settle.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_hum.narration: A cub folds one ear toward your hum. The cubs settle into a furry heap, and Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum, but the cubs are asleep.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_beat.narration: Sefa taps softly under your beat. The cubs settle into a furry heap, and she mouths thank you. Your packs still hum, but the cubs are asleep.

interaction_cub_lullaby_response_word.narration: A cub yawns your word back at you. The cubs settle into a furry heap, and Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum, but the cubs are asleep.

interaction_lost_moths_response_hand.narration: A moth lands on your thumb and stops shaking. Then they all rise and fly south, glowing steady. Ahead, the ground turns soft and muddy.

interaction_lost_moths_response_hum.narration: The moths lean toward your hum and glow brighter. Then they all rise and fly south, glowing steady. Ahead, the ground turns soft and muddy.

interaction_lost_moths_response_dim.narration: The moths settle into your cupped hands like birds in a nest. Then they all rise and fly south, glowing steady. Ahead, the ground turns soft and muddy.

voiceGuide.tone: wide-open, warm and a little uneasy; a homeland that is quietly rearranging itself around the stones

npcVoices.sefa_tallgrass: pride elder; voice like warm gravel; formal and kind; says 'east of the river, wave first'; quietly worried about the cubs
npcVoices.cart_driver: a caravan driver from Stone Crossing; indignant about pride escort bookings; very fond of his donkey
npcVoices.waystation_centaur: a road-warden centaur re-embroidering sashes; talks around spools of thread; tuts a great deal; precise about roads
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, six people in matching brass hats; trying out a toll rope of their own; smooth until asked a simple question
npcVoices.bracken_swiftmile: a relay-running centaur stuffed with letters; quick, cheerful, competitive; 'relay waits for nobody'
npcVoices.manticore_cubs: two manticore cubs who pretend to be rocks; giggly, honest, dream the ground is singing
npcVoices.granny_ash: a manticore grandmother with a famous spiced grass-cake nobody finishes; bossy, delighted by everything
npcVoices.marker_movers: two polite manticores moving a pride marker post further from the caravans, again

interaction_plates.narration: Granny Ash's cake is the pride's welcome, and the whole pride lines up along a long table for it. "Pass the plates down!" she calls. "Gently! Cake this spicy has opinions." The plates go hand to hand, and the cubs cheer every one.

interaction.cue: Catch the plate, then pass it down the table.

onSuccess.narration: Every plate arrives, and not one slice jumps off. Granny Ash tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

onFailure.narration: One plate wobbles, and a cub catches the cake on his head. He wears it proudly. The line laughs, and the plates go on.

onAssisted.narration: Granny Ash passes every other plate herself, and not one slice jumps off. She tucks a honeycake into your pack. "For later," she says. "Something normal."

interaction_post_hole.narration: The manticores have the post at its new hole at last, and it leans over the hole like a tired giraffe. "Hold it straight," says the bigger one, "while somebody stamps the earth in."

interaction.cue: Friends hold the post upright while someone stamps the earth in.

onSuccess.narration: The post goes in straight the first time. The manticores tie a fresh tuft of tail-fur on top and say it is the neatest move all month. The smaller one pays you three coins from the pride jar. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

onFailure.narration: The post goes in slightly crooked. The manticores tilt their heads, decide crooked is fine, and tie a fresh tuft on top. "It still says keep away," one of them says.

onAssisted.narration: The bigger manticore holds the post straight herself, and it goes in first time. They tie a fresh tuft of tail-fur on top, and the smaller one pays you three coins from the pride jar. "Hole-digging wages," she says. "Do not tell the Brassbuckles."

interaction_cub_lullaby.narration: The cubs need a soft sound. Each hero adds a hum, a gentle beat or a sleepy word. Make it aloud if you like. Sefa keeps the cubs' tails from drumming on the bowls. That part is harder than it looks.

interaction.cue: Each hero adds something to the bedtime song.

options.label: Hum softly
options.reaction: A cub folds one ear toward the hum.

options.label: Tap a very gentle beat
options.reaction: Sefa taps softly underneath your beat.

options.label: Offer a sleepy word
options.reaction: A cub repeats your word into a yawn.

onSuccess.narration: The cubs settle into a furry heap. Sefa mouths thank you. Your packs still hum; the song has helped the cubs, not silenced the stones.

onFailure.narration: Sefa joins the song until the cubs settle.

onAssisted.narration: Sefa holds the tune while you add quiet sounds. The cubs sleep with everyone's help.

interaction_lost_moths.narration: The glowing river has gone, but a handful of little moths got left behind. They huddle in the grass, flickering, too scared to fly south by themselves.

interaction.cue: Help the lost moths feel safe until they glow steady again.

options.label: Hold out a warm hand
options.reaction: A moth lands on your thumb and stops shaking.

options.label: Hum very softly
options.reaction: The moths lean toward the sound, glowing a little brighter.

options.label: Cup your hands around the glow
options.reaction: The moths settle into the shadow, like birds into a nest.

stages: They lift off together, heading south.

onSuccess.narration: The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.

onFailure.narration: The moths rise together and go south after the others, glowing steady. The grass is quiet. Ahead, the ground turns soft.
